propositions: Duplicate allowlisted read-only tool calls (read_file, search_files, list_directory, show_ticket) waste 40-70% of request budget by re-executing identically and re-paying round-trips; memoization at the agent-call seam returns cached results without re-executing.

Error-prefixed results (e.g., 'Error: cannot read') are not memoized and re-execute on retry; deterministic sentinel-empty results (e.g., '(no matches)', '(empty)') are memoized as stable, honest answers.
Nudge escalation steers models away from duplicate loops: first repeat carries level-1 static nudge, subsequent repeats level-2 text; byte-stable templating preserves prompt-caching guarantees.
Runaway guard observes every memoized duplicate and still trips the abort backstop at the same call index; wrapper order is guard (outermost) → memo → steering (innermost).

Memoization is keyed on tool-call signature with identical normalization to the existing usage_log distinct-ratio actuator; non-deterministic and write tools (record_criterion_verdict) are exempt from the allowlist.
Live Bedrock capture proves nudge-broken loop arrest: identical duplicate calls memoized to single execution while guard observes both signatures; model emits final answer after nudge intervention.
